subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Second-Order Systems: Oscillation and Damping
description: A micro-lesson that makes Second-Order Systems: Oscillation and Damping usable.

hook.text: A car hits a bump and the suspension bounces. How many bounces depends on the damping ratio.

buildup.text: A second-order system has two poles. The damping ratio ζ determines the shape of the response.

discovery.text: ζ < 1 is underdamped — oscillation. ζ = 1 is critically damped — fastest without oscillation. ζ > 1 is overdamped.

twist.text: Most control systems target ζ around 0.7 — fast response with only a small overshoot.

climax.text: Speakers, bridges, and servo motors are all modeled as second-order systems for design.

punchline.text: Two poles, one damping ratio — ring, creep, or land perfectly.

quiz.question: What damping ratio gives the fastest response without oscillation?
